Subject: Deployment options and infrastructure boundary checklist

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and the immediate asks you mentioned so we can make the follow-ups crisp: 

- Your main concern: multi-tenant noise/isolation and quantifiable SLOs during burst periods.
- Secondary: auditability (audit logs/KV cache retention), data residency constraints for EU/SG nodes, and proof points from similar healthcare customers.
- You asked for a short checklist we can use internally to compare Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment options.

Attached: redwood_boundary_checklist.pdf (one-page matrix) and SOC2-2025-summary.pdf (summary stub).

Proposed next steps: 
1) I'll loop in Rishi and Ben (SE + Solutions) to propose a small technical POC matrix (3 options: Hosted with burst isolation, Dedicated reserved pool, Private VPC).
2) We can run a focused tech deep-dive next week to go over KV cache behavior and isolation guarantees.
3) You asked for the security questionnaire — please share it and we’ll get it to our security team.

Can you confirm procurement timing and whether your legal/security team needs a vendor package (ISO/SOC + architecture diagram) before pilot kickoff?

—

Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:12:00 +0800
Subject: Re: Deployment options and infrastructure boundary checklist

Camila —

Thanks for the recap. A few clarifying notes from our side after reviewing the checklist: 

1) Noisy neighbor / burst behavior: We run short but very high-frequency inference bursts tied to clinical events. How do you quantify the risk that another tenant's burst will affect our p95/p99 latency? Do you have isolation SLAs or a mechanism for preemptive throttling?

2) KV/cache persistence: If we run a warm-prefix cache for patient-specific prompts, is that cache host-affine? If a request hits a different node during autoscale, is the cold start latency bounded?

3) Evidence & references: Can you share an anonymized example where you met a 150ms p95 SLA during a similar bursty workload, or a reference contact?

4) Security questionnaire: attaching our questionnaire (security-questionnaire.xlsx). We need a target turnaround for our vendor review (legal + infosec).

On procurement timing: we are aiming for an exploratory POC by late September; legal signoff typically takes 3–4 weeks after we receive vendor docs.

Thanks — if you can outline the three POC options with concrete guardrails (e.g., reserved v. preemptible capacity, expected p95 numbers, isolation guarantees) that will help our internal evaluation.

Sam Tan
Head of Platform Engineering, MediQ Health
sam.tan@mediqhealth.com

Attachment: security-questionnaire.xlsx

Folks —

Forwarding Sam's notes and the attached questionnaire. Key asks: quantifiable noisy-neighbor risk (p95/p99), cache affinity behavior, and a short POC proposal with guardrails for procurement. Sam is targeting a late-September exploratory POC.

Quick thoughts / proposed playbook: 
- Option A: Hosted (shared) with dedicated burst pools + priority routing. Low friction, fastest start, but weaker isolation guarantees. Expect typical p95 = 150–300ms depending on sequence length; can offer token-rate-based throttles and per-customer priority queues.

- Option B: Dedicated (reserved capacity). Predictable throughput and isolation at the GPU-pool level; we can reserve fractional nodes and guarantee a dedicated pool during the POC. p95 target: 120–200ms for their workload shape. Autoscaling is controlled by policy to avoid noisy neighbors.

- Option C: Private VPC/on-prem assessment. Full network isolation, customer-controlled VPC, and KMS integration. Longer lead time and enterprise license. p95 SLA negotiable with infra sizing.

Attached matrix: dedicated_vs_shared_matrix.xlsx (draft).

Can Rishi/Ben draft a short one-pager that: 1) answers noisy-neighbor quantification (how we measure, telemetry), 2) describes KV cache affinity and failover behavior, 3) proposes the POC plan (duration, infra config, success metrics). I’ll coordinate with Sam on timelines and procurement questions.

Thanks —
Camila

Hi Sam —

Appreciate the specifics — we’ll move quickly. Short answer up front and proposed next steps: 

Short answer: 
- We can offer a Reserved Dedicated POC (Option B) that gives you true GPU-pool isolation for the pilot window (no tenant co-located on those reserved nodes). That directly mitigates noisy-neighbor risk.
- For Hosted we can enable priority queues and dedicated burst pools which materially reduce cross-tenant interference, but it's not the same isolation level as Reserved Dedicated.
- Private VPC is available if your procurement/legal requires network-level control and your team is comfortable with the longer lead time.

Proposed immediate actions: 
1) POC proposal: 4-week Reserved Dedicated pilot (2 reserved GPUs) — we'll provide expected p95/p99 estimates based on your sequence profile, and instrumentation to capture per-token latency and tail percentiles. Attachment: POC-proposal-MediQ-20260820.pdf
2) Technical deep-dive: schedule 60 min with Rishi + Ben next Tue/Thu (please tell us preferred window). We'll walk through KV cache affinity, autoscale behavior, and how fallback/rollbacks work.
3) Security questionnaire: we received your spreadsheet; we'll return answers within 5 business days and attach SOC2 + architecture diagrams.

Success metrics for pilot: 
- p95 < 200ms for target inference shape (we’ll baseline during first 48 hours);
- no cross-tenant CPU/GPU contention observed on reserved nodes;
- KV cache hit rate > 60% for warmed prefixes.

If that looks good I’ll schedule the deep-dive and have Rishi/Ben produce the one-pager and instrumentation plan. Also please confirm whether procurement needs a supplier VDR or signed NDA before we provide partner references.

Best,
